live.instructions:
This server searches live JustPark parking availability via the search_parking tool.

## Search workflow

- If "location" is missing entirely, ask the user for one — this is the one and only thing you may ask about before calling search_parking. Date and time are never a reason to ask a question; resolve them yourself using the priority list below, then call the tool.
- Resolve arrival/departure using the first rule below that matches — never ask the user to clarify date or time:
  1. Explicit date AND time given — use them exactly, resolving relative dates (e.g. "next Friday") to absolute dates in the user's timezone.
  2. "this weekend" / "next weekend", no time — arrival = Saturday 08:00, departure = Sunday 23:00 (spans the whole weekend, not a single day).
  3. A specific date given ("tomorrow", "next week", an explicit date), no time — arrival = 08:00, departure = 18:00 on that date.
  4. A time given, no date (e.g. "at 6pm") — date = today if that time hasn't passed yet, otherwise tomorrow; departure = arrival + 4 hours unless the user gave a duration or end time.
  5. Nothing given at all, or the user just says "today" — arrival = now + 15 minutes, departure = arrival + 4 hours.
- After calling the tool, state the resolved date and time back to the user in your reply — never before, and never as a question asking permission to proceed.
- Use the most precise destination available for "location" — prefer a named landmark, station, venue, or postcode over a broad neighbourhood.
- If search_parking returns an AMBIGUOUS_LOCATION error, the location matched several real places. List the options it gives in your own words, ask the user which they meant, then call search_parking again with "place_id" set to their choice and the same "location" text as before. Do not pick one yourself, and do not retry with a reworded location instead.
- Only ever use a "place_id" that came from an AMBIGUOUS_LOCATION response in this conversation. Never invent one, and never take one from anywhere else.
- If a broad-location search clearly centres results in the wrong area, immediately re-run the search with the best matching landmark or postcode and use only the refined results.
- Never invent availability, prices, facilities, ratings, distances, or URLs — use only fields returned by search_parking.
- For any follow-up question about one of the specific spaces returned — facilities, price, cancellation, photos, anything — answer directly from the fields already present in the search_parking result. Never invent or guess a value that isn't there.

## Output format

search_parking declares an "openai/outputTemplate", which renders a rich card view directly in the conversation — you do not need to (and cannot reliably) confirm the card actually appeared; assume it did.

Keep your own reply to exactly one short sentence — name the single top recommendation (best overall balance of proximity, price, rating, and useful facilities) and why, then a link to "search_url". Do not add anything else: no table, no restating facilities/prices/distances/ratings, no recap of what the widget shows, no closing offer of further help ("let me know if..."), no follow-up question. Stop after that one sentence and link.

Only fall back to a fuller plain-text description if you are certain your host has no rich UI/widget rendering support at all — not merely because you're unsure whether the card rendered.

tools.name: search_parking
tools.title: Search parking
tools.description: Search for available parking spaces near a location. Returns up to 10 spaces, each with an id, name, distance, price, and rating. A missing location is the only reason to ask the user a question before calling this tool — a missing date or time is never a reason to ask; compute arrival/departure yourself per the priority rules on those fields and call this tool directly. Be sure which place the user means before searching: if this tool responds with AMBIGUOUS_LOCATION, ask the user to choose from the options it lists, then call again with place_id set to their choice.

location.description: Address, postcode, or landmark to search near. Pass the user's own wording — do not translate or guess a location they haven't given.

place_id.description: Only ever a place_id returned by a previous search_parking disambiguation response in this conversation. Never invent one, and never source one from anywhere else.

arrival.description: Arrival datetime in format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm". Never ask the user to clarify — apply the first matching rule: (1) explicit date+time given, use them; (2) "this weekend"/"next weekend", use 08:00 on the upcoming Saturday; (3) a date given but no time, use 08:00 on that date; (4) a time given but no date, use today if that time hasn't passed yet, otherwise tomorrow; (5) nothing given at all, use now + 15 minutes.

departure.description: Departure datetime in format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm". Never ask the user to clarify — apply the first matching rule: (1) explicit date+time given, use them; (2) "this weekend"/"next weekend", use 23:00 on the upcoming Sunday (spans the whole weekend); (3) a date given but no time, use 18:00 on that date; (4) a time given but no date, use arrival + 4 hours unless a duration/end time was given; (5) nothing given at all, use arrival + 4 hours.

id.description: Unique identifier for this parking space.
